notes: Expected retrieval numbers for the synthetic CI fixture (account 9001,
The eval job fails if dense precision@5 or recall@10, or either number
for a list under `candidates`, drops more than `tolerance` below these
values. Rising numbers never fail the gate. `candidates` scores what the
resume builder hands the model (app/evals/candidates.py): skills by name,
projects by repository, over the 8 skill_evidence pairs.
These are a canary for retrieval breaking, not a quality measurement:
the data behind them is invented. See the header of ci_fixture.yaml.
To update deliberately, when a change legitimately moves the numbers:
run `make eval-fixture`, confirm the new numbers are what the change
should have produced, copy them into `dense` or `candidates` below, and say in the
commit message which change moved them and why the new value is right.
Never update this file to make a red build go green without that.
tolerance_reasoning: Absolute, not relative, and applied to each metric separately.
Measured rather than guessed. Seeding and scoring were repeated three
times on one machine; once more after deleting the database and the
Qdrant collections so every vector was recomputed from the model; and
once on a GitHub Actions runner, a different operating system, CPU and
Python build. All five runs returned the same floats, bit for bit, to
the last digit of a double. Against a Qdrant server and against
qdrant-client's local mode the ranked ids and their order matched too;
only the cosine scores differed, in the sixth decimal place, which is
far too small to reorder anything here.
So the tolerance is not absorbing observed noise, because there is
none. It is set below the smallest move either metric can make: with
13 pairs, one document changing places in one pair's top-k moves
precision@5 by 0.2/13 = 0.0154 and recall@10 by at least 1/4 relevant
ids /13 = 0.0192. At 0.01 the gate therefore fails on any single
document that stops being retrieved, and is non-zero only so that it
tests ranking rather than float equality.
One caveat worth knowing before trusting a red build. This project's
dependencies are declared with floors and resolved fresh on every run,
so a torch or sentence-transformers release can change these vectors
without a line of this repository changing. Until the dependency tree
is pinned, check what moved before assuming the code did.
